events.summary: Sri Lanka reduced selected fuel prices from midnight on 31 March.
Pekoe Trail development proceeds with European Union financial support.
India and Sri Lanka agreed to review bilateral project progress quarterly.
Minister ordered measures to prevent detained boats obstructing Mayilitti harbour operations.
Sinopec planned contracts and construction after doubling the proposed refinery capacity.
Development Lottery Board reported a 13 percent increase in Presidential Fund contributions.
Sri Lanka launched an online reporting system for child sexual abuse material.
Northern Province governor authorized an investigation into spoiled World Bank seed potatoes.
Government reduced rice import tax temporarily to clear customs-held stocks.
President instructed officials to reopen the National Art Gallery by year-end.
President instructed officials to build a theatre at Colombo’s Sudarshi complex.
President ordered preparation of a comprehensive report for a national cultural zone.
Government proposed sanitary-pad vouchers for approximately 800,000 schoolgirls.
President opened the German-Sri Lanka Friendship Maternity Hospital in Karapitiya.
Government advanced plans to establish a National Higher Education Development Commission.
Sri Lankan prime minister planned final negotiations on debt restructuring during China visit.
President announced bills to establish a digital transactions agency and artificial intelligence centre.
Government allocated one billion rupees from the 2024 budget for digital institutions.
Minister planned to submit Cabinet paper seeking electricity charge relief for Northern farmers.
Government decided to provide 20 kilograms of rice to 2.8 million low-income families.
Minister announced two new Badulla-route services and a tourist observation train.
2024 school food programme began for primary students nationwide.
Government allocated Rs. 16.6 billion to nine provincial councils for school meals.
Cabinet approved digitisation of the entire foreign employment sector.
Minister announced plans to digitise foreign employment services through an integrated migrant-worker application.
Central Bank announced a Treasury bill auction scheduled for 27 March.
Consumer Affairs Authority will publish imported-goods prices and VAT daily.
Government allocated Rs. 26 billion for school lunches for 1.7 million students.
IMF agreed to provide Sri Lanka’s remaining financing under the programme.
Paddy Marketing Board received Rs. 1 billion for Maha-season paddy purchases.
The Paddy Marketing Board spent Rs. 95 million purchasing paddy over five days.
President opened the new accident and emergency unit building.
President handed over 234 acres for cultivation by Jaffna farmers.
Land deeds were distributed to 408 people under the Urumaya programme.
Sri Lanka and IMF reached agreement ahead of approval for the third EFF tranche.
Eastern Province Governor donated Rs. 500,000 to the Presidential Gaza Children’s Fund.
Government planned a special empowerment programme for 14,000 Aswesuma beneficiaries.
Cabinet approved accelerated information collection for the Urumaya land-title programme
Cabinet approved a nationwide programme to create one million young entrepreneurs
Education Ministry and Microsoft signed an artificial-intelligence school pilot agreement
India pledged financing for comprehensive development of Kankesanthurai Port
Women-led plastic recycling network received electric bicycles in Batticaloa
India agreed funding to begin Kankesanthurai Port development.
School bus donated to Mahinda Rajapaksa College in Matara.
Presidential scholarship application deadline extended to April 1.
Presidential Fund allocated scholarships for 100,000 students.
Construction began on 1,300 Indian-funded plantation worker homes.
Sri Lanka Railways built an open-top carriage for future hill-country tourist services
Government agencies plan a mobile app to coordinate beach-cleaning activities
Sri Lanka approved two Adani wind projects in Mannar and Poonery
Sri Lanka’s energy minister signed a power-purchase agreement with Adani Green Energy
India pledged Rs. 250 million to complete Kaduruwela Trilingual National School
Officials released biological controls to contain coconut whitefly disease in Mannar.
Importers agreed to sell onions at controlled prices during the festive period.
President agreed to allocate funds for paddy purchases across districts.
President proposed appointing experts to study and report on construction-sector problems.
China offered funding for Northern Province housing, rice and fishing support.
India offered funding for Northern Province development and marine initiatives.
Japan offered funding for Northern Province development and maritime security.
Finance Ministry extended applications for the second Aswesuma welfare phase.
Homes with utilities were handed over to fire-affected plantation families.
Government announced a land-rights programme for 176,000 plantation families.
Homes handed over to 24 fire-affected families at Olirud Estate.
Serin River Park project estimated at Rs. 440 million.
Serin River Park opened for public use in Holuwagoda, Galle.
Power purchase agreement signed for Hambantota 150 MW solar project.
RDA began 14-day rehabilitation of Central Expressway section.
China donated bomb-disposal machinery and protective equipment to Defence Ministry.
Sri Lanka Railways moved all reserved seat bookings online.
Experts are planning a modern deep-sea fishing vessel for sustainable fisheries.
Authorities will select an investor to develop Galle as a tourism port.
Agriculture minister said egg price controls would be imposed if producers refuse reductions.
Colombo canal rehabilitation and flood-control works were accelerated across multiple sites.
Agriculture ministry allocated funds for home gardens exceeding ten perches.
Fisheries minister submitted a Cabinet paper proposing volunteer sea scouts.
Prabhasam programme provided smart classroom equipment to a Gampaha school.
President proposed recruiting 2,500 English-medium teachers, including 1,000 retirees.
Authorities released 40.9 acres of military-held land in Kilinochchi District.
India pledged 1,200 houses through two housing projects in Southern Province.
India is implementing two housing projects across 50 Southern Province villages.
Finance Ministry approved 4,500 officers for elephant-fence protection.
Government announced second-phase Aswesuma payments from June.
Government allocated Rs.205 billion for Aswesuma payments this year.
Minister opened Vekve Solar’s solar power plant in Orumulacholai.
Vekve Solar provided Rs. 500,000 for school infrastructure.
Finance Ministry approved assigning 4,500 officers to protect elephant fences.
Forest Conservation Department began using drones to investigate forest fires.
National Water Supply Board introduced emergency hotline 1939 for supply complaints.
Prabhasam programme provided a bus to Kinniya Central College.
Military-held land was returned to owners in Jaffna and Kilinochchi.
Government announced paddy purchases would begin the following day.
Government planned to import 40 million eggs before the festive season.
Lanka Sathosa reduced prices of four essential goods nationwide.
Government proposed the 2024/2025 President's Scholarship Programme.
Education reforms proposed establishing 20 additional zonal education offices.
Special trains began operating on Northern and hill-country routes for the long weekend.
President ordered expedited housing provision for all homeless Kajimawatta families.
Minister set electricity reconnection fee at Rs. 800.
New electricity connection fees would be payable through instalments after initial payment.
Sri Lanka Post signed a strategic collaboration agreement with UPS.
Finance Ministry decided monthly disability and kidney patient allowance payments.
Government planned China-assisted construction of 2,000 homes near Colombo.
India signed an agreement to fund Northern Islands electricity generation development.
Nationwide English, information technology and guidance training launched for 25,000 A-Level students.
Authorities began actions to make four Sri Lankan beaches operational under Blue Flag standards.
Transport minister announced plans to deploy 200 electric buses, beginning with 50.
Officials took steps to restart passenger ferry service between Sri Lanka and Nagapattinam.
Cabinet approved increasing the school meal cost per student to Rs. 110.
Education Ministry launched free vocational training for Advanced Level students.
Motor vehicle department services began operating through a digital registration system.
President ordered immediate action to start 26 agricultural modernisation projects.
Pilot agricultural modernisation projects had started in 26 divisional secretariats.
Each selected divisional secretariat received 25 million rupees for agricultural modernisation.
AI teaching pilot was planned for 20 schools from March 19.
Applications opened for the 2024/25 President’s Scholarship Programme.
President’s Fund allocated Rs. 3.6 billion for the scholarship programme.
Military agreed to release 164 acres in Jaffna and Kilinochchi.
Sapugaskanda refinery will temporarily shut for 45 days from July.
Thai Buddhist group donated $50,000 for the President’s Fund poverty-relief programme.
